name: Basantapur (Kathmandu) Durbar Square
description:
Location and Existence:
Enlisted in World Heritage Sites by UNESCO, Kathmandu Durbar Square is
a historically and culturally significant site located in central
Kathmandu. Although the construction of the square began in the 3rd
century, the major structures within it were added in later periods.
The outer complex consists of a number of 16th century temples built
during the reign of the Malla kings. The complex consists numerous
temples, palaces and chowks constructed from the reign of King Ratna
Malla till the reign of King Prithvi Bir Bikram Shah Dev.
Descriptions:
Durbar Square is the area surrounding several temples and courtyards,
including:

a. Basantapur Tower (Nautale Durbar)

b. Gaddi Baithak

c. Kumari Chhen (Ghar)

d. Trailokya Mohan Narayan Temple

e. Kasthamandap

f. Maju Dega Temple

g. Shiva Parvati Temple

h. Bhagawati Temple

i. Taleju Bell and Two big drums

j. Shwet Bhairav

k. Dega Taleju Temple

l. Vamsha Gopal (Krishna) Temple

m. Jagannath Temple

n. Kaal Bhairav

o. Indrapur Temple

p. Narayan Temple

q. Kageshwor Mahadev Temple

r. Kotilingeshwor Mahadev Temple

s. Maha Vishnu Temple

t. Taleju Bhawani Temple

u. Makhan Pashupatinath Temple

v. Hanuman Dhoka Palace and Museum
Basantapur Tower (Nautale Durbar)

The Basantapur Tower is the tallest structure in Kathmandu royal
palace, the Hanuman Dhoka. Standing nine-stories high, the building is
variously referred to as the Nautale tower, Basantapur Tower or simply
Basantapur. It is one of four corner towers and do not house any
deities as they were constructed by King Prithvi Narayan Shah and King
Pratap Singh Shah from 1768 to 1775, to symbolize the elder's
unification of the valley.
Gaddi Baithak

In 1965, Prime Minister Chandra Shumsher Rana built the Gaddi Baithak
in Rana period style by replacing the Malla period style during
renovation. At that time, the Gaddi Baithak was used to welcome
foreign guests, give certificates of rank, and hold important state
meetings. Currently, it is used as a part of Basantapur museum.
Historical weapons, pictures of various events that give a political
introduction to Nepal from the unification to the republic, and old
pictures can be seen in these sections.
Kumari Chhen

The Kumari Ghar is a three-storey Newari-style building with rich and
detail wood-carving and detail woodcarving which symbolize gods,
located near Gaddi Baithak and Trailokya Mohan temple. This is
residence of Living Goddess, Kumari, a young newar girl who is
considered as reincarnation of Goddess Durga. The Kumari Ghar was
built during the reign of King Jaya Prakash Malla in 1757, as a
remorseful act by King to overcome his guilt toward particular sexual
indiscretion girl. The place is well known for its magnificent art of
carving and divine living.
Trailokya Mohan Narayan Temple

This temple is an elegant three-tiered temple set on a five-story
plinth that exists near Kumari Chhen (Bahal), on the north of
Shiva-Parvati temple. Built in 1679 by Parthivendra Malla to honor his
dead brother, Nripendra Malla, the 'Trailokya Mohan' means 'Vishnu of
the three worlds', so also known as 'Temple of the ten incarnations of
Vishnu,'. Some years later, in 1689, Nripendra's widow Riddhi Laxmi
sponsored the installation of a votive Garuda statue, depicted
kneeling in an attitude of prayer toward the temple's west façade.
Kasthamandap
Kasthamandap (Newari: मरु सत; literally
\"wooden covered shelter\") is a three-story public shelter that
includes a sacred temple for Gorakhnath in the Basantapur Durbar
Square. It is located just behind the Trailokya Mohan Temple. Laxmi
Narasingh Malla is credited with having Kasthamandap built in early
16th century, while an inscription has been found that it was built
by a person named Biseta. The word 'Kasthamandap' comes from the
Sanskrit language, meaning a wooden pavilion. It is said that the
necessary wood to build this pavilion have been derived from a single
tree. The oldest written mention of the word 'Kasthamandap' can be
found in the \"Namasangiti\" text written in the 12th century Bikram
Samvat. The Newari word for Kasthamandap is \"Maru Sata\", meaning a
shelter covered with wood. In the Pushpika Nepal Mandala, a collection
of old manuscripts written in the late 20th century, Kathmandu is
referred to as Kasthamandap Mahanagara. Mahanagara means \'great
city\'. The city is still called Kasthamandap by Buddhist monks and
priests. That is why Kathmandu is also called Kasthamandap. Ashok
Vinayak locally known as Maru Ganesh exists near this Kasthamandap.
Maju Dega Temple
The Maju Dega (or Mahadeva) is an
imposing three-tiered Newari-style temple-tower, dedicated to Shiva,
standing on a hefty pyramidal plinth, located near to Shiva-Parvati
temple and opposite to Gaddi Baithak. Built in 1690, it was
constructed by Queen Riddhi Laxmi during the reign of her grandson,
Bhupalendra Malla, who had the misfortune of dying at age 21 after
taking the throne at the tender age of 8.
Shiva Parvati Temple
The Shiva-Parvati temple is located on
the southwest side of the square. It is a rectangular, two-story
building, facing south, standing directly northeast of the much larger
Maju Dega temple. The temple was constructed at the tail end of the
18th century during King Rana Bahadur Shah's rule. The monument is
widely characterized as the Shiva-Parvati temple as the upper level
features a pair of mannequins of Shiva and Parvati, seemingly gazing
south across the square. The temple's formal name is Navadurga,
referring to 9 manifestations of the goddess durga. The platform on
which the temple stands was originally a dabali platform, a stage used
for masked dances and performances.
Bhagawati Temple
The Bhagawati temple is located near the southwest corner of Hanuman
Dhoka palace adjacent with Gaddi Baithak. Facing west towards the
street, it stands opposite to Shiva-Parvati or Navadurga temple. It is
one of the few structures attributable to Jagajjaya Malla, who ruled
Kathmandu from 1722-36. The temple is built as a five-level monument
with two brick ground floors surrounded by three tiers of Newar-style
roofs. The structure originally housed a statue of the god Narayan,
Mahipatindreshwor, named after the King Mahipatendra Malla. But later
it was stolen in 1767 and never returned. In its place, King Prithvi
Narayan Shah raised an image of Bhagawati that he had taken from
Nuwakot. Despite this, the statue is temporarily returned to its
original place in Nuwakot for a short time each April-a tradition that
continues today.
Taleju Bell and two big drums
 
Adjacent to Shiva-Parvati temple and opposite to Bhagawati temple, big
Taleju bell exists which was erected by King Rana Bahadur Shah in
1797. The bell is rung 108 times and two big drums are beaten during
the everyday worship ceremony of 'Taleju Bhawani'. So, the bell is
popularly known as Taleju Bell.
Shwet Bhairav

Shwet Bhairav is a statue of Bhairav, avatar of Shiva located in
Hanuman Dhoka. Shwet Bhairav depicts the most dangerous and fierce
face of Lord Shiva. The mask of Shwet Bhairav is so fierce looking
that locals out of fear keep it inside a wooden frame window, and only
one frame is opened for the devotees except for a special day; Indra
Jatra when all windows are opened. Inside the wooden latticed screen,
below Dega Taleju is hidden the terrifying face of Shwet Bhairav. The
giant structure was fashioned and installed in 1795, during the rule
of King Rana Bahadur Shah.
Dega Taleju Temple

Dega Taleju is the second tallest temple after Taleju temple in
Basantapur Durbar Square. It is located adjacent to Hanuman Dhoka
Durbar. Constructed in 1564 by King Mahendra Malla, the temple is
dedicated to Goddess Taleju Bhawani. The temple's architectural
design, influenced by Goddess Taleju's divine instructions, resembles
a Yantra, a sacred geometrical design representing the universe.
Perched atop a pedestal in Durbar Square, the temple's grandeur is
striking. However, access to its inner sanctum, housing shrines of
Taleju Bhawani and Kumari Devi, is restricted. Only Kings were
historically allowed entry, but during Dashain, the ninth day permits
Hindu devotees to offer prayers directly. Other visitors can
appreciate the temple's exterior beauty and significance.
Vamsha Gopal (Krishna) Temple

Also locally known as 'Chyasilin Dega', the octagonal temple is
located to the northwest of the square. It was constructed in 1648
during the reign of King Pratap Malla. It memorializes Rupamati and
Rajamati, two of Pratap Malla's queens, and also houses an inscription
extolling Pratap Malla's military campaigns. In front of the main
entrance are two stone pillars, one of which is capped by a
west-facing image of Hanuman in an advanced state of disrepair.
Jagannath Temple

Located just in front of Hanuman Statue, also known as Char Narayan,
Jagannath Temple was built during the reign of King Mahendra Malla in
1563. Later, an image of Krishna was installed during the reign of
King Pratap Malla. The monument is a Newar-style temple built of brick
and wood atop a low plinth. At each of the four corners, set apart
from the main building, are small two-tiered subsidiary towers. It has
been renovated multiple times after earthquakes. Just in front west of
Jagannath temple, there is small two-storey Laxmi Narayan temple.
Kaal Bhairav

Located west in front of Indrapur and Narayan temple, Kaal Bhairav is
a Hindu black 12ft. huge stone statue of Bhairav, which is enshrined
in the temple, is said to have been sculpted in the 5th or 6th
century and was later rediscovered in a paddy field in 17th century
and later it was placed at the Durbar Square by King Pratap Malla.
Indrapur Temple

Indrapur is a sattal-like temple with an open plan upper level,
directly adjacent to the Vishnu or Narayan temple. Unusually, it
defies the typical convention that forbids worshippers from occupying
a floor above the enshrined deity, though in recent years, access to
the balcony has been restricted. The upper level was occasionally used
to display a statue of Indra during the annual Indrajatra festival.
Narayan Temple

Located between Kageshwor temple and Jagannath temple, Narayan Temple
is a stunning three-tiered monument perched atop a four-level base.
The temple is believed to have been built in the late 17th or early
18th century. The three-story temple may appear impressive from the
outside, but the interior is only inhabitable on the ground floor. The
base features a square cella, topped with an interior ceiling, while
the upper levels are purely decorative and inaccessible.
Kageshwor Mahadeva Temple

The Kageshwor is a square temple on the northern side of Kathmandu
Durbar Square. Originally known as the Bhuvanalaksmewor (after its
benefactor, Queen Bhuvanalakshmi), it now serves as a substitute for
the temple of the same name about 14 km to the northeast. This was one
of the last temples of note constructed in Durbar Square, erected
c.1711. Prior to 1934 it was Newar-style monument, probably with two
or three tiers of roofs. However, the 1934 earthquake destroyed the
upper levels, which were rebuilt in the Shikhara style.
Kotilingeshwor Mahadeva Temple

The Kotilingeshwor Mahadeva Temple stands on the northwest side of the
square, directly southwest of Mahavishnu Temple. Built in 1562 by King
Mahindra Malla, it is one of the earliest surviving Shikhara style
temples. However, its present appearance vastly understates the impact
of its 16th century form as its Shikhara-style towers were hastily
replaced with small domes following an earthquake in 1746. The
shikharas were never rebuilt. The temple's central image is a
four-faced statue of Shiva in the form of a chaturmukha linga.
Maha Vishnu Temple

Located near Kotilingeshwor temple and opposite to Kageshwor temple,
Maha Vishnu temple was built during the reign of King Jagajjaya Malla
(1722-36) in the memory of his son Rajendra Malla. It was probably
built as a royal memorial temple. One may surmise that over time, as
memory of Jagajjaya Malla and his lost son faded, the temple gradually
transformed into a generic place of worship for Maha Vishnu himself-a
role that continued into the 20th century.
Taleju Bhawani Temple

Located just behind east of Kageshwor Mahadev temple, dedicated to
Taleju Bhawani, the large Taleju Bhawani Temple was built in 1564 by
Mahendra Malla. Later it was renovated in the 1650s or 1660s during
the reign of King Pratap Malla. The current layout of the temple
resembles a cosmic mandala. The main building, with three tiers of
roofs, stands upon a twelve-stepped base. Around the sanctuary are 16
satellite shrines designed as two-level Newar-style towers. The roofs
of the main building are covered by gilt copper sheets and are
supported by carved wooden struts depicting a variety of deities. The
temple's perimeter is surrounded by a high wall and the Singha Dhoka
(Lion Gate) built by Pratap Malla is opened for public during Indra
Jatra.
Makhan Pashupatinath Temple
Located at the north of the durbar square, Makhan Tole, this temple
was built by King Mahendra Malla. Locally known as 'Makhan Pashupati'
or 'Sano Pashupati', it was built for the devotees who are unable to
visit Pashupatinath. Like original Lord Pashupatinath temple in
Devpatan, has a five-faced Shiva lingam and a basah inside the temple
on the east side.
Hanuman Dhoka Palace and Museum
Hanuman Dhoka Palace was originally founded during the Lichchhavi
period (4th to 8th centuries A.D.). The eastern wing with ten
courtyards is the oldest part dated to the mid-16th century. The
royal family lived in this palace till 1886. They after shifted to
Narayanhity Palace. Currently the palaces are used as Hanuman Dhoka
Palace Museum, dividing its sections as Tribhuwan museum, Mahendra
museum and Birendra museum, where stone carvings, impressive thrones,
jewel-studded ornaments used for coronations, weapons, wooden
furniture, coin collections, paintings, royal personal commodities,
etc. are displayed.
Hanuman Gate
The Hanuman Gate is located on the west side of Durbar Square. It is
the entry gate to the palace, where a standing statue of Hanuman
(monkey god), dated to 1672, guards the palace. Hanuman is decked with
a red cloth and an umbrella. The face is smeared with a red paste. On
the left is a stone sculpture dated to 1673 of Lord Narasimha, which
is credited to King Pratap Malla period according to an inscription on
the pedestal of the image.
Nasal Chowk
Ahead of the main entrance, Nasal chowk courtyard is located. The
courtyard was built during the Malla period, the buildings around it
were built during the Rana regime. The Panch Mukhi Hanuman temple
dedicated to Hanuman is in the northeast corner of the Nasal Chowk.
Coronation ceremony and other royal social rituals are performed in
this chowk.
Mul Chowk
Mul chowk, dedicated to Taleju Bhawani, is a courtyard with two-storey
buildings all round that are exclusive places for religious rites.
During the Dashain festival, the deity of Taleju is shifted to this
temple.
Mohan Chowk
Mohan Chowk, built in 1649 to the north of Nasal Chowk, was the
residential courtyard of the Malla kings. It was mandatory for a Malla
king to be born here to become heir to the throne. At the center of
the courtyard, there is a golden waterspout, known as Sundhara, said
to be spring sourced from Budhanilkantha.

name: Kathesimbhu Stupa
description:
The Kathesimbhu Stupa is located in central Kathmandu, about 650m
north of the Hanuman Dhoka Durbar Square. Although commonly thought to
date from the mid-17th century, the earliest inscription found here
dates from 1551 and the stupa was repaired during the reign of King
Pratap Malla. The stupa is also called Shree Gha-Shanti Ghat
Bajradhatu Mahachaitya. The site as a whole is a miniature replica of
the Swayambhunath, complete with the small Harati Mata outbuilding in
the northwest corner of the courtyard. It is said that it has been
built for those who are unable to reach to Swoyambhunath.

name: Seto Machchhindranath
description:
Seto Machchhindranath, aslo known as Janabaha Dyo, Karunamaya, is a
deity worshipped by both Hindus and Buddhists in Kathmandu. The temple
of Seto Machchhindranath is located in Jana Bahal. Located at Keltole
between Asan and Indra Chok in central Kathmandu, the temple is
believed to have been established around the 10th century. The 32
hands tall chariot procession festival of Seto Machchhindranath is
celebrated during the month of Chaitra.

name: Indra Chowk
description:
Indra Chowk, also known as Wongha, is one of the ceremonial and market
squares on the artery passing through the historic section of
Kathmandu. The intersection of Indra Chowk, along with Maru, Kathmandu
Durbar Square, Makhan, Jana Baha, Asan and Naxal, mark the old
India-Tibet trade route that is now a vibrant market street. The large
temple of Akash Bhairav on the western side of the square is the
symbol of Indra Chowk. The temple houses a large mask of Akash
Bhairav, which means 'god of the sky', up a flight ofs tairs. The
ground floor contains shops.

name: Ranipokhari
description:
Location & Existence:
Ranipokhari, originally known as Nhu Pukhu, is a historic artificial
pond located in the heart of Kathmandu. To the east of Rani Pokhari
exists 'Ghantaghar' or 'Clock Tower' built by Rana Prime Minister Bir
Shumsher and Tri-Chandra College whereas to the south exists Ratnapark
and to the west exists Nepal's first School, 'Durbar High School'. The
square-shaped tank dates from the 17th century, and was built on the
eastern side of the then city limits. It lies just outside a former
city gate. Rani Pokhari was built in 1670 A.D. by King Pratap Malla to
console his queen who was distraught with grief after their son
Chakravartendra Malla was trampled to death by an elephant.
Descriptions:
The pond, which is 180 meters long and 140 meters wide, covers an area
of ​​62 ropanis and 13 aanas. The pond is recharged by water flowing in
through an underground channel, but there are also 7 wells inside the
pond. A temple dedicated to Bal Gopaleshwor Mahadev or Yamaleshwor,
stands at the center of the pond. There is an idol of HariShankari. It
is reached from the street by a causeway. A large stone statue of an
elephant bearing the images of Pratap Malla and his two sons
Chakravartendra Malla and Mahipatendra Malla is situated on the tank's
southern embankment. There are 4 smaller temples situated at the 4
corners of the pond.

name: Dharahara (Bhimsen Tower)
description:
Dharahara or Bhimsen Stambha, is a 72m tall tower at
the center of Sundhara, Kathmandu. It was first built in 1832 by
Muktiyar or Prime Minister Bhimsen Thapa under the commission of Queen
Lalit Tripurasundari. The tower had a spiral staircase containing 213
steps. The eighth floor held a circular balcony for observers that
provided a panoramic view of the Kathmandu valley. Actually the first
tower was built in 1824 at his residence, Janarala Bagh, situated at
south-east of Sundhara, near Bhotebahal of Kathmandu. It got torn in
half during 1834 earthquake and was never rebuilt. Later second
dharahara was built, along with the Sundhara. Later the first Bhimsen
tower was completely destroyed in 1934 earthquake and never rebuilt,
only second dharahara was reconstructed.
2015 earthquake again devasted the second dharahara and third tower
has been constructed in the same premises nearby the remains of old
dharahara, extending the premises area. The newly rebuilt Dharahara
stands as a 22-story structure with modern features. It includes a
museum, a garden and a fountain nearby, along with two lifts and
underground parking. It retains the traditional minaret shape and has
a bronze mast on the roof, similar to the original design.

name: Ratnapark
description:
Ratna Park is a park located in central
Kathmandu. It is named after Queen Ratna, wife of King Mahendra. It
was built for children and named after the gem. King Mahendra had the
park prepared for children as per the plans of the then Queen Ratna
Rajyalakshmi. Construction began in 2018 and was completed in 2021.
The park is named after the planner Ratna and her statue was also
installed. It is located in the central part of Kathmandu between Rani
Pokhari and Tundikhel. The statue of Ratna Rajyalakshmi in the middle
of the park was vandalized by protesters in 2062/63 BS. The Kathmandu
Metropolitan City changed the name of the park to Shankhadhar Udyan in
2077 BS, along with the installation of a statue of Shankhadhar
Sakhwa.

name: Thamel
description:
Thamel is a commercial neighborhood located in Kathmandu. The name
comes from 'Tha Bahi', indicating its root origin to have come from
Newar community. The Bahi has been the center of the tourist industry,
starting from the hippie days. It is known for its narrow alleys
crowded with various shops and vendors. Many restaurants, hotels,
lodges serve traditional and continental cuisine and warm stay. It is
widely popular for its nightlife.

name: Garden of Dreams
description:
The Garden of Dreams, also known as Garden of Six seasons, is a
neo-classical garden in Kaiser Mahal, Kathmandu built in 1920. It is
located in Kaiser Mahal which is across the street from the former
Royal Palace at the entrance to the Thamel tourist area. Designed by
Kishore Narsingh, it consists of 6,895 sq. m. of gardens with three
pavilions, an ampitheatre, ponds, pergolas and urns. Each of the six
pavilions, which provide the Garden's architectural framework, is
dedicated to one of the six seasons in Nepal.
It was one of the most sophisticated private gardens of that time
designed by Kishore Narsingh for Field Marshall Kaiser Shumsher Rana.
After the death of Kaiser Shumsher, the garden was handed over to the
government of Nepal, but it was not properly managed for decades.
Later, it was recently restored with the help of Austrian government
and declared it open to the public with a new name 'Garden of Dreams'.
Today, only half of the original garden remains. Kaiser library also
exists adjacent to it.

name: Narayanhity Palace Museum
description:
The Narayanhity Palace Museum is a public museum in Kathmandu located
next to Keshar Mahal. The former royal palace is being used as museum
in 2008 where the royal personal commodities and rooms are displayed.
Before the revolution, the palace was the residence and principal
workplace of the monarch of the kingdom of Nepal.
The existing palace complex was built by
King Mahendra in 1963 and incorporates an impressive array of
courtyards, gardens and buildings. Ownership of the palace site
changed multiple times prior to being occupied by the monarchy.
Initially, Prime Minister Fateh Jung Shah used to live on the property
before rana regime. Then it was taken over by Rana Prime Minister Bir
Shumsher and new palace for King Prithvi Bir Bikram, was constructed
by demolishing the old palace. Then later, after 1934 earthquake. King
Mahendra demolished the old palace and constructed a new existing one
with floor space of 3,794 sq. m.

name: National Museum (Chhauni)
description:
National Museum, located at the base of Swayambhunath,
is the first museum of Nepal. The museum has a rich history, initially
serving as an Arsenal house constructed in 1824 by Prime Minister
General Bhimsen Thapa. In 1926, Rana Prime Minister Chandra Shumsher
added two wings to the north and south of the main building and
renamed it Silkhana Museum. Later, in 1938, Rana Prime Minister Juddha
Shumsher renamed it Nepal Museum and opened its door to the public on
February 12, 1939. As the museum has evolved, its name has also
changed. Later on, in 1968, it was renamed the National Museum, which
renames popular to this day.
Covering an area of approximately 50 Ropani, the museum comprises
various buildings, gardens and open spaces within its premises. Its
primary function is to preserve and exhibit rare and valuable art
treasures. The classical building of the museum is on the western side
of the river Vishnumati against a hilly background. Entering the
museum, on the left is the Art Gallery displaying statues, wood
carvings and paintings. The building straight ahead is the Buddhist
Art Gallery displaying Buddhist art objects while the building on the
right is the Museum of Natural History displaying different animals
and birds of Nepal's biodiversity. The Military section is a
collection of weapons and artifacts from ancient, medieval and modern
Nepal. The Numismatic section preserves rare copper, silver and gold
coins and paper notes from the Lichchhavi era until modern times.

name: Pashupatinath Temple
description:
Location and Existence:
Located in central Kathmandu, on the bank of Bagmati River,
Pashupatinath Temple is the oldest Hindu temple in Kathmandu,
dedicated to Pashupati, a form of Shiva. Enlisted in the World
Heritage Sites by UNESCO, the Pashupati complex is spread over the
total area of 246 hectares. It is a living heritage and the Bagmati
River has further enhanced the glory of this holy place, where rituals
from birth to death are performed.
Regarding its origin, Pashupatinath Temple's existence is recorded as
early as 400 CE. According to Gopalraj Aalok Vhat, the temple was
built by Prachanda Deva, a lichchhavi king. Another chronicle states
that Pashupatinath Temple was in the form of Linga shaped Devalaya
before Supuspa Deva constructed a five-storey temple of Pashupatinath
in this place. As time passed, the temple needed to be repaired and
renovated. It is known that this temple was reconstructed by a
medieval king named Shivadeva (1099-1126 CE). It was renovated by
Ananta Malla adding a roof to it. Further temples have been erected
around the two-storied temple, including the Vaishnava temple complex
with a Rama temple from the 14th century and the Guheswari temple
mentioned in a 11th century manuscript, overtime.
Descriptions:
The complex includes 518 mini-temples and a main pagoda temple, along
with cremation area and its forest area. The main temple is built in
Newari architecture. The two-level roofs are of copper with gold
covering. The temple rests on a square base platform with a height of
23m 7cm from base to pinnacle. It has four main doors, all covered
with silver sheets. This temple has a gold pinnacle. The sacro
sanctrum, or the main idol, is a stone Mukhalinga with a silver yoni
base bound with a silver serpent. It is one meter high and has 5
faces, which represent 4 aspects of Shiva; Sadyojata, Vamadeva,
Tatpurusha, Aghora and Ishana.
The other important temples are Guheswori temple, Virupakshya temple,
Gorakhnath temple, Kirateswor temple, etc. There is 'Mrigasthali ban'
forest of deer and 'Kripalu Udhyan' garden too inside the complex.
There are many festivals throughout the year among them Maha
Shivaratri and Teej are the most celebrated one and a lot of devotees
visit the temple.

name: Swoyambhunath
description:
Location & Existence:
Enlisted by UNESCE in World Heritage Sites, Swoyambhunath is an
ancient religious complex atop a hill in the Kathmandu valley, west of
Kathmandu city. Swoyambhu, meaning 'self-sprung' in Nepal bhasa, for
the Buddhist newars, it occupies a central position, most sacred
Buddhist pilgrimage site.
According to Swoyambhu Purana, the entire valley was once filled with
an enormous lake, out of which grew a lotus. The valley came to be
known as Swoyambhu, meaning 'self-created'. The name comes from an
eternal self-existent flame over which a stupa was later built.
According to the Gopalarajavamsavali, it was founded by the great
grandfather of King Mandeva (464-505 CE), King Varsadeva, about the
beginning of the 5th century CE. This seems to be confirmed by a
damaged stone inscription found at the site, which indicates that King
Varsadeva ordered work done in 640 CE.
Later, in 15th century, the reconstruction of the stupa was done
during the reign of Malla King and the eastern stairway was
constructed in 17th century during reign of King Pratap Malla.
Later, the Swoyambhu Shrine was re-gilded using 20kg of gold.
Descriptions:
The stupa consists of a dome at the base, on top of which is a cube
structure, painted with eyes of Buddha looking in all four directions.
There are pentagonal toranas present above each of the four sides of
the cube with Buddha reliefs on them. Behind and above the toranas
there are 13 tiers. Above all the tiers there is a small space above
which the Gajur is present. There are 5 gilt Buddha shrines at the
base of the stupa, all with a Buddha statue inside them. There are
several Chaityas and Harati Maata Mandir in the complex. Swoyambhunath
is popular as 'monkey temple' among the tourists because there are lot
of monkeys live in that area. Swoyambhunath is sacred pilgrimage site
for both Hindus and Buddhists.

name: Bouddhanath
description:
Location, Existence & Descriptions:
Bouddhanath Stupa, also known as 'Khasti' in newari language, is a
stupa and major spiritual landmark seen as the embodiment of the
enlightened mind of all Buddhas, located 11km northeast of Kathmandu
valley. Enlisted in World Heritage Sites by UNESCO, It is filled with
consecrated substances, the stupas' dome has a diameter of 100 ft.,
stands 141.16 ft. tall and spans 1 hectare, and its massive mandala
covering approximately 6,756 sq. m., makes it the largest spherical
stupa in Nepal.
Regarding its origin, an earlier written source Gopalarajavamsavali
says Bouddhanath itself was founded by the Nepalese Lichchhavi King
Shivadeva (c.590-604 CE); though other Nepalese chronicles date it to
the reign of King Manadeva (464-505 CE). There is a legend regarding
its origin dated back to the reign of King Manadeva. According to the
history of Nepal, there was no sign of water in Narayan Hity built in
the southern part of the Narayanhity Palace, for which King Dharmadeva
consulted astrologers. Astrologers suggested that a sacrifice with a
male candidate having 32 perfections, should be performed. Only the
king himself and his 2 princes were suitable candidates. So, the king
ordered his son to behead the person sleeping by covering face without
looking his face. And the son did so and realized that he had killed
his own father. With regret for salvation, he flew a rooster hen and
it landed in the place where the chaitya is currently standing. And he
started for the construction of this stupa. During the time of its
construction, the place was struck with a drought and it that was
built by collecting the droplets of dew, which is called 'khasu ti' in
newari. So the stupa is known as 'Khasti' in newari. However, it a
sacred pilgrimage site for Tibetan Buddhism and Newar Buddhism.

name: Budhanilkantha Temple
description:
Budhanilkantha Temple is situated below the Shivapuri Hill at the
northern end of the Kathmandu valley. It is located in Budhanilkantha
municipality of Kathmandu district. It is about 10km from Tribhuwan
International Airport. Also known as the Narayanthan Temple for Hindus
and 'Bhuija-shi Narayan' in Newari language, and can be identified by
a large reclining statue of Lord Mahavishnu. The name means "Old Blue
Throat", a title of god Shiva. According to legend the spring that
feeds the pond in the Budhanilkantha temple is connected to
Gosainkunda which makes it to have a direct connection to the water
source from Shiva. This is the reason why its name is dedicated to
Shiva even though the statue is dedicated to Vishnu since the water
pond on which the statue lies, has its source to Gosainkunda dedicated
to Shiva which was the result of him drinking the poison and storing
it in his throat resulting in him having blue throat.
Regarding its origin, there is no fixed evidence. Devmala chronicles
says that King Shirasavdeva enshrined that huge statue. Other legend
says that, it was enshrined by king Haridatta barma. The main statue
is carved up on a single block black basalt stone. The statue stands
5m tall and is positioned in the middle of a recessed pool of water,
which is 13m long. The statue is believed to be more than 1400 years
old. Thousands of devotees visit the site during Haribodhani Ekadashi
and Harishayani Ekadashi.

name: Balaju (Baisdhara) Park
description:
Location, Existence & Description:
Balaju Park, also known as Baisdhara, is a tranquil and popular
leisure spot located approximately 5 km northwest of Kathmandu under
the Nagarjuna forest. Balaju Garden offers a harmonious blend of
natural beauty and artistic elements, making it an attractive
destination for tourists.
Regarding its origin, though the area exists from Lichchhavi period, a
lot of monuments and parks were developed in different time period.
Around 875 Nepal Sambat, King Jaya Prakash Malla initially established
21 stone taps (dhungedhara). King Pratap Malla built a replica of
Budhanilkantha in a pool filled with sacred water at this park. Later
in 1855 B.S, King Rana Bahadur Shah added 1 dhungedhara and the place
got its name Baisdhara. Later the park was constructed from 2021 B.S.
and was opened to public.
Descriptions:
The major attractions of the park are 22 dhunegdhara, replica of
Budhanilkantha, beautiful garden, artistic ponds and natural beauty.
Spread over 162 ropanis, the area also has religious importance during
festivals.

name: Tribhuwan Park
description:
Tribhuwan Park is a popular public park located at the south-west
corner of Kathmandu in Thankot. Established in 1972 by the late King
Birendra in honor of his grandfather, King Tribhuwan, the park covers
an area of 1.3 sq. km. and is a popular destination for educational
tours, school picnics, corporate picnics and family gatherings. The
park offers a beautiful view of the surrounding area, with an angelic
green sod and picnic spot. It is a great palce to enjoy the serene
environment and greenary beauty, lying in the shade of the Chandragiri
Hills.

name: Jal Binayak (Koina Ganesh), Chobhar
description:
Location:
Jal Binayak is a Hindu temple of Lord Ganesh located on the west bank
of the Bagmati river, a watercourse that defines the eastern border of
Kirtipur. It is located immediately downstream of the scenic Chobhar
gorge. It is one of the four Binayak of Kathmandu Valley.
Existence and Description:
The temple was built initially in 723 Nepal Sambat by King Shiva Singh
Malla. After 83 year the Gajur was added to the top of the temple in
789 N.S. by King Sri Nivas Malla of Patan. The present structure of
the temple was reconstructed in Pagoda style in 871 N.S. by King Rajya
Prakash Malla of Kathmandu. Jal Binayak is manifestation of Ganesh,
represented here as a god emerging from the tip of a large boulder
measuring 1.5\*3 meters.

name: Taudaha
description:
Location and Existence:
The name, Taudaha Lake, comes from a combination of Newari words 'Ta',
meaning snake and 'Daha', which means lake. It is situated at about
6km southwest from Lagankhel, in Kathmandu district. The lake is
believed to be about 86 ropanis, 4 hectares which is 500m long and
400m wide, with a depth of about 5 to 10m and is uneven in shape with
8 corners and situated at an altitude of 1350m above sea level.
Description:
According to mythology, a Buddhist mythical character Manjushree cut
the hill in the valley's south, allowing the lake's water to drain
off, thereby creating land for settlement. After the water of the
ancient lake drained away, a few small lakes and ponds were created
beyond the hill. Taudaha is believed to be one of those ponds. However
since the lake is the residence of many snakes and Karkotak Serpent,
even today fishing and swimming are prohibited in Taudaha. The lake is
natural habitat for many aquatic animals and migratory birds. Every
year, a big fair is held in Taudaha on the day of Nag Panchami.

name: Shesh Narayan, Pharping
description:
Location:
The temple is one of the four Narayan temples, located near the
ancient town of Pharping, which lies approximately 20km south-west of
Kathmandu.
Existence:
It is believed that the main temple was built in the 17th century
but the cave to the right has been a place of pilgrimage for far
longer. There are some artfully carved Lichchhavi era statues in the
courtyard, including lively depictions of Garuda and Hanuman.
Description:
There are five small ponds below the temple. One of the surrounding
ponds is bluish which is always mysterious and called as Basuki Kunda,
which flows into the other surrounding ponds. The Basuki Kunda has
piles of bamboos and wooden poles which is a result of a rituals
observed during Haribodhani Ekadashi, in the month of Kartik, falls on
the 11th day of Shukla Paksha.

name: Pharping Hydropower Station, Soukhel Pharping
description:
Location:
Pharping Hydropower Station is the Nepal's first and Asia's second
oldest power station which is located in Pharping of Kathmandu
district, nearly 13km south from Kathmandu.
Existence:
The construction work was started in 1907 A.D during the prime
ministership of Rana Prime Minister Chandra Shumsher and the power
station was inaugurated by the late king Prithvi Bir Bikram Shah Dev
on Monday, 22 May, 1911 (B.S 1968, 9 Jestha) at 6:30 pm by switching
on lights in Tundikhel, Kathmandu.
Description:
The power station was established as Chandrajyoti Hydro-electric power
station by Chandra Shumsher and after taken over by Nepal Electricity
Authority, it was renamed as Pharping Hydropower Station. It was
erected with a grant from British Government at a cost of NRs. 0.713
million and involvement of 950,000 manpower.
The power station utilizes spring water from Kutali River, Satmule and
Shesh Narayan area channelized from a 200m high dam constructing a
circular water reservoir. The diameter of the reservoir is 200ft, 18ft
depth and capacity is 528,733cu. Ft. There are two units each with a
rated capacity of 250kw totaling installed capacity of the power
station to be 500kw.
The power produced from the hydropower project was used mostly to
light houses and palaces of the elite Rana families. The line was
connected in a local house of Madan Krishna Maharjan at Khokana to
test the safety before hooking up wires in palaces.
The electricity had been generated till 2038 B.S. Even 110 years after
the construction, this hydropower project can generate electricity.
However, currently the electricity generation has been halted and
water from the reservoir is now channeled for drinking water supply to
the local residents of southern part of Lalitpur. A master plan has
been prepared to develop the site as 'Live Energy Museum' and opened
for public since 2010.

name: Dakshinkali Temple
description:
Location:
The Dakshinkali temple is situated southwest part of Kathmandu at a
distance of 22km from Kathmandu, 1 km away from the village of
Pharping. The temple is set at the confluence of two sacred streams in
a rocky cleft in the forest.
Existence:
The surreal Dakshinkali temple is an ancient place which has unique
tales behind its establishment. It is believed that the Goddess Kali
appeared in a dream of the Malla ruler who reigned over Nepal in the
14th century. The goddess supposedly ordered the king to construct a
temple which would be devoted to her. The king then set out to follow
her orders immediately, and the temple was built with an image of the
deity carved out from stone positioned in the shrine. It is also said
that King Pratap Malla built the temple during 17th century. It is
also said that the temple was built in 1855 by Rani Rashmoni, a
devotee of Kali.
Description:
The Dakshinkali derives its name from a compound of the words
'Dakshin' which means 'south', and the name 'Kali', which means
'fearful form of Goddess Parvati'. Dakshinkali is typically shown with
her right foot on Shiva's chest. The idol of the goddess Kali is
embellished with a sword in one hand, a skull cap in another, and a
severed head in the third, the four-armed idol represents an image of
a strong, empowered divine being who has arrived to conquer evil and
emerge as victorious. A pathway leads off from behind the main temple
uphill to the small Mata temple on the top hill, which offers good
views over the forest.
Religious Importance:
The fame of this temple lies in its rituals and traditions. The temple
is one of the favorite Hindu pilgrimage destinations. Twice a week,
Saturday and Tuesday, animals are sacrificed at this place-uncastrated
male goats and cockerels in particular as an offering to the goddess.
During the annual celebrations of Dasain the temple is washed by a
crimson tide and the image of Kali is bathed in the gore.

name: Sundarijal
description:
Sundarijal is a village, part of Gokarneshwor Municipality, Kathmandu.
It is located 15km northeast of Kathmandu. The name Sundarijal was
derived from the term 'sundari' and 'jal' which means beautiful water.
Sundarijal is also considered the gateway to the Shivpuri Nagarjuna
National Park. This VDC, which also includes a large part of the
Shivpuri Nagarjuna National Park, is also a major watershed for
drinking water consumed in the Kathmandu Valley. Northern portion of
Sundarijal is the forest that belongs to Shivapuri National Park.
Sundarijal covers an area of 5.18 sq. km. The Bagmati River flows
through the village, where tributary rivers Shyalmati and Nagmati
confluence with Bagmati River. Sundarijal VDC also houses Nepal\'s
second hydroelectric power plant, Sundarijal Hydropower Plant. This
hydroelectric power plant with a capacity of 640 kilowatts was built
in 1992 BS by the then Rana Prime Minister Juddha Shamsher. The main
gate of the Melamchi Drinking Water Project, which is said to be
brought to meet the acute shortage of drinking water in the Kathmandu
Valley and to fulfill that shortage, is also located in this VDC.
Krishna Temple and Ganesh Temple are located just a few meters away
from Sundarijal Bus Park, the main entry point to Sundarijal.
Similarly, Sundarimai Temple, which has become the symbol of this VDC,
is located a few km away from Sundarijal Bus Park, along the way to
the park. This temple is visited by devotees for 9 days during
Dashain, the great festival of Hindu Nepalis. It is famous for its
natural beauty, picnic spot and habitat for many species of plants and
wildlife animals and birds.

name: Bagh bhairav, Kirtipur
description:
Location:
The Baghbhairav temple, located 7km southwest of the Kathmandu valley,
is located at an altitude of 1405 meters above sea level, 50 meters
long and 30 meters wide. The Baghbhairav temple, spread in the middle
of the kirtipur hill, which is spread in an east-west shape, is the
largest and most important temple in this area.
Existence:
Kirtipur was founded by King Shivadev III between Nepal Sambat 219-246
(AD 1099-1126) as mentioned in the Gopal Raj Vansavali. The
Baghbhairav temple, which is believed to have been built with the
establishment of Kirtipur city, is believed to have a history of about
900 years. No records are found regarding the temple until Nepal
Sambat 623. It is said that the temple was renovated grandly by
Jagatpal Varma, the great ruler of Patan, in the month of Kartik,
Nepal Sambat 635. Thereafter, 43 years after Prithvi Narayan Shah
conquered the Nepal Valley, it is mentioned that Rana Bahadur Shah's
maternal grandmother Hastikala renovated the temple in Nepal Sambat
923.
Description and legend:
It is a three-storey pagoda style temple with a copper roof on the top
and two lower roofs covered with thatch. The temple has 18 gajurs, 11
on the top, 1 in the middle and 1 at the bottom. Scenes from the
ancient Mahabharat and Ramayana can be seen on the ground floor of the
temple.
According to mythological folklore, in ancient times, there was a
forest where the temple is now located. Shepherd children who went to
graze sheep and goats in the northern forest slopes made a statue of
tiger while making various clay statues. After the statue of the tiger
was made, they went to find leaves to make a suitable tongue for it.
During that time, Bhairav appeared in the statue of the tiger and ate
the sheep and goats, they started crying. Later, when they saw that
the mouth of the tiger statue they had made was stained with blood,
they did not put their tongue on the statue out of anger, saying that
the same tiger had eaten their sheep and goats. Later, there is a
legend that a temple was built and the statue was placed there, saying
that God originated in the statue. Based on that legend, it is
believed that the statue of Bagh Bhairav does not hav a tongue to this
day.
This temple holds a Baghbhairav Jatra every year on Singh Sankranti
(Bhadra 1). It is customary to perform khat jatra on the occasion of
jatra. The tradition of performing khat jatra started on Bhadra 1,
2014 B.S.

name: Adinath Lokeshwor , Chobhar
description:
Location & Existence:
Chobhar village is located 6km southwest from Kathmandu. The temple is
revered by both Buddhist and Hindu pilgrims. Adinath Lokeshwor Mandir
was built in 15th century, then rebuilt in 1640. In this village, in
8th century Indian Buddhist nun Gelongma Paloma (Bhikshuni Srimati)
started to practice Nyung Ne ritual.
Description:
Adinath Lokeshwor is honoured by Buddhists as a form of the
Bodhisattva and by Hindus as Surya. Six figures of the Buddha are
lined up beneath the temple's golden torana. His temple in Chobhar
stands at the highest point of the village on a site already in use in
Lichchhavi times.
The shikhara-style shrine in front of the temple has a Shiva lingam
and is also said to be the entrance to a cave leading through the
mountain to the Chobhar Gorge. The frontage is decorated with pots,
pans and water jugs hung there by young couples seeking to ensure a
happy marriage.

name: Patan Durbar Square
description:
Location & Existence:
Patan Durbar Square, listed in UNESCO world heritage site, is situated
at the center of Patan, Mangal Bazaar. Though the authentic history of
Patan Durbar Square is not clear, the chronicles says that the durbar
was established during the reign of Thakuri King Laxmikam Deva dated
1024 to 1040 B.S. Later, the Malla kings made important changes to the
square and reform the locality. Most of the current architecture is
from 1600s constructed during the reign of malla kings that include
Siddhi Narsingh Malla, Srinivas Malla, Sivasimha Malla, Vishnu Malla
and Yoganarendra Malla.
Descriptions:
Durbar Square is the vicinity of many temples and courtyards that
include:

1. Patan Durbar Square 2. Patan Museum

b. Bhimsen Temple b. Keshav Narayan Chowk

c. Vishwanath Temple c. Mul Chowk & Taleju Temple

e. Hari Shankar Temple e. Bhandarkhal Garden
